title: Toxic ammonia: {value} free NH₃
message: Free (un-ionised) ammonia is {value}. Above 0.02 ppm it damages gills; fish may gasp, clamp fins or hide.
advice: Change 30–50% of the water now, temperature-matched and dechlorinated.
Stop feeding for 24 h and remove anything decaying.
Retest ammonia in 12–24 h.

title: Ammonia very high: {value}
message: Total ammonia is {value}. The filter is not keeping up (new tank, overfeeding, a dead fish or a cleaned filter).
advice: Large water change today.
Check for a dead fish or rotting food.
Do not clean the filter media now.

title: Ammonia detected: {value}
message: A cycled tank should read 0. Its toxicity rises with pH and temperature; see Free Ammonia.
advice: Feed less for a few days.
Retest in 24 h; change 25% of the water if it stays.

title: Imbalance after water change
message: Ammonia is {value} {daysAfter} days after a {percent}% water change. Something keeps producing it.
advice: Change water again urgently (30–50%).
Watch the fish closely for the next days and retest daily.
Look for the source: dead fish, decaying plants, overfeeding, filter stopped.

title: Ammonia rising
message: Ammonia went up by {change} ppm in 3 days (now {value}).
advice: Check the filter is running and was not over-cleaned.
Reduce feeding.

title: Nitrite high: {value}
message: Nitrite blocks oxygen transport in the blood (brown gills, gasping).
advice: Change 30–50% of the water now.
Retest daily until it reads 0.

title: Nitrite detected: {value}
message: A cycled tank should read 0 nitrite.
advice: Feed less and retest in 24 h.
Change 25% of the water if it does not drop.

title: Nitrate high: {value}
message: Long-term nitrate above 40 ppm stresses fish and feeds algae.
advice: Increase water change size or frequency.
Check for overfeeding and dead spots in the substrate.

title: Nitrate very high: {value}
message: Above 80 ppm nitrate becomes harmful to most fish.
advice: Do two 30% water changes a day apart.
Test your tap water: it may already carry nitrate.

title: Nitrate low for plants: {value}
message: Planted tanks usually need 5–20 ppm; below 5 plants can yellow from the old leaves and algae can win.
advice: Check your fertilizer dose includes nitrogen.

title: Nitrate building up
message: Nitrate rose by {change} ppm in a week (now {value}).
advice: Water changes are not keeping up: change more or more often.
Feed less.

title: pH {value}: watch the neons
message: pH is above 7.5. Neon tetras prefer soft, acidic water; watch for faded colour, clamped fins or hiding.
advice: Check CO₂ is running (pH rises when it stops).
Do not chase pH quickly with chemicals; stability matters more.

title: pH low: {value}
message: Below pH 6.0 the nitrifying bacteria slow down, so ammonia can build up.
advice: Check KH: a low buffer lets pH fall.
Test ammonia.

title: pH swinging by {change}
message: pH moved by {change} within 24 h. Swings stress fish more than a steady value.
advice: With CO₂ injection a drop of ~1 during the light period is expected; more than that, reduce CO₂.
Check KH.

title: KH very low: {value}
message: Below 2 dKH (~36 ppm) the water has almost no buffer and pH can crash, especially with CO₂.
advice: Water change with your tap water.
Reduce CO₂ until KH is back up.

title: KH low: {value}
message: Under 3 dKH (~54 ppm) pH becomes unstable.
advice: Watch pH swings.
Avoid large CO₂ increases.

title: CO₂ high: {value}
message: Calculated CO₂ above 30 ppm can make fish gasp at the surface.
advice: Watch the fish at the end of the light period.
Lower the bubble rate a little.
Compare with the drop checker (lime green = ~30 ppm).

title: CO₂ dangerous: {value}
message: Above 40 ppm CO₂ fish can suffocate.
advice: Turn the CO₂ down now and add surface agitation.
Note: the KH/pH formula overestimates CO₂ if other buffers (e.g. phosphate) are present.

title: CO₂ low for plants: {value}
message: Calculated CO₂ is under 15 ppm; plants grow slowly and algae get the upper hand.
advice: Check the bubble counter and the CO₂ canister.
Drop checker should be lime green by the time the lights are on.

title: Temperature high: {value}
message: Above 28 °C the water holds less oxygen and fish metabolism speeds up.
advice: Check the heater thermostat.
Add surface agitation; in summer use a fan over the water.

title: Temperature low: {value}
message: Below 22 °C most tropical fish get sluggish and prone to disease.
advice: Check the heater works and is the right size for the tank.

title: Temperature changed by {change}
message: Temperature moved by more than 2 °C within a day.
advice: Match new water temperature during water changes.
Check the heater.

title: Oxygen risk: warm water and high CO₂
message: Warm water holds less oxygen and CO₂ is high at the same time.
advice: Reduce CO₂ and add surface agitation.
Watch for fish at the surface.

title: Oxygen low: {value}
message: Under 5 ppm dissolved oxygen fish breathe faster; under 4 it is dangerous.
advice: Increase surface agitation or add an air stone at night.
Check the filter flow.

title: Chlorine detected: {value}
message: Any chlorine kills beneficial bacteria and burns gills.
advice: Add dechlorinator for the whole tank volume now.
Always dose dechlorinator before or with new water.

title: GH low: {value}
message: Under 3 dGH (~54 ppm) plants and snails can run short of calcium and magnesium.
advice: A GH remineraliser or a Ca/Mg supplement raises it.

title: GH high for soft-water fish: {value}
message: Above 12 dGH (~214 ppm). Neons and other soft-water fish live longer in softer water.
advice: Mix in RO or rain water at water changes if your fish need it.

title: Phosphate high: {value}
message: Above 3 ppm phosphate fuels algae, especially with weak light or CO₂.
advice: Reduce phosphate dosing and feeding.
Test the tap water.

title: Phosphate low for plants: {value}
message: Under 0.1 ppm plants can stall and green spot algae appears on slow leaves.
advice: Check the fertilizer includes phosphate.

title: Nitrate-limited (NO₃:PO₄ = {ratio})
message: Nitrate {num} vs phosphate {den}. A ratio under 5:1 favours cyanobacteria (blue-green slime).
advice: Add nitrogen or reduce phosphate; aim for about 10:1.

title: Phosphate-limited (NO₃:PO₄ = {ratio})
message: Nitrate {num} vs phosphate {den}. A ratio over 30:1 favours green spot algae.
advice: Add phosphate or reduce nitrogen; aim for about 10:1.

title: Iron high: {value}
message: Above 0.5 ppm iron can feed algae and harm shrimp.
advice: Pause iron dosing until it drops.

title: Iron low for plants: {value}
message: Under 0.05 ppm new leaves can come in pale (chlorosis).
advice: Check the micro-nutrient fertilizer dose.

title: Potassium low: {value}
message: Under 5 ppm older leaves get pinholes and yellow edges.
advice: Increase the potassium part of the fertilizer.

title: Silicate high: {value}
message: Above 2 ppm silicate feeds brown diatom algae.
advice: Common in new tanks and fades; otherwise check the tap water and substrate.

title: TDS climbing: {change} in 30 days
message: Dissolved solids keep rising (now {value}); minerals and waste are accumulating.
advice: Larger or more frequent water changes bring it back down.

title: {param} is {status}: {value}
message: {param} is outside the ideal range you set.

title: Weekly water change due
message: Last water change was {days} days ago. Your routine is 15–20% weekly.
advice: Use "I want to do a water change" on the Aquarium screen.

title: No water change in {days} days
message: It has been over 2 weeks since the last water change.
advice: Change 20–30% now, then return to weekly.

title: Filter clean due in a week
message: The filter was cleaned {days} days ago; the 3-month cleaning is coming up.
advice: Plan it a few days away from a water change, so the bacteria recover.

title: Filter clean due
message: The filter was cleaned {days} days ago (every 3 months).
advice: Rinse the media in removed tank water, never tap water.
Clean pipes and strainers at the same time.

title: Time to test: {params}
message: Not tested for over a week: {params}.
